message.reasoning:
We need to imagine three experts, each propose one test case for each method, share, etc. But final output must be a single JUnit4 test file covering typical use cases, edge cases, error scenarios. Include tests for constructor? methods: elements(), addElement(), removeChild (inherited), submit(), formData(). Also test behavior of submit when action missing, baseUri, method POST/GET, etc. Use Jsoup library? Since we are testing FormElement, we can instantiate a FormElement with a Tag and Attributes. Tag can be Tag.valueOf("form"). Attributes using new Attributes(). Need to import Jsoup classes. For submit, we don't want actual network connection; Jsoup.connect returns a Connection object; we can mock Jsoup.connect static method using PowerMock or we can test that submit throws IllegalArgumentException when action missing and baseUri empty. For typical case, set baseUri and action attribute, then submit returns a Connection with correct URL and method.

But mocking static Jsoup.connect is complex. Maybe we can test that submit returns a Connection with the expected URL and method without performing network call, by using Jsoup.connect which returns HttpConnection (real) but we can set a dummy URL, it won't be executed. So test that connection.request().url() matches action, and method matches GET/POST.

We need to ensure no network call. Jsoup.connect will not attempt until execute, so safe.

Test formData: create form with various elements: input text, checkbox unchecked, checkbox checked, radio, select with selected option, select without selected, disabled input, input without name. Use addElement to add elements.

Also test elements() returns internal Elements list.

Test removeChild: add child element, remove using removeChild, ensure it's removed from elements list.

Edge cases: submit when action attribute empty and baseUri empty => expect IllegalArgumentException.

Also test that addElement returns same FormElement (chaining).

Construct test file with @Test methods.

Use JUnit 4 annotations.

Will need to import org.jsoup.nodes.*, org.jsoup.parser.Tag, org.jsoup.Connection, org.jsoup.helper.HttpConnection, org.jsoup.helper.Validate, org.jsoup.select.Elements, org.jsoup.Jsoup.

Also need to create Attribute via new Attributes(). add("action","http://example.com/submit") etc.

Also need to create Elements: we can use new Element(Tag.valueOf("input"), "", new Attributes()).

Set attributes like name, type, value, checked etc.

Implement helper method createInput.

Ok produce final test file.

Start and end markers.
